title: 23rd Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with 32 members present. The government's Zakat Bill had its first reading, then members debated three committee reports. The Economic Committee's report on the Maldives Intellectual Property Office Bill drew short, mostly supportive speeches. The Finance Committee's report on a special audit of Maldives Ports Limited diesel purchases (2018-2020) led to a long, heated exchange between government and opposition members over corruption and who is accountable. The Environment and Climate Change Committee's report on a Water and Sewerage Act amendment drew speeches on the deadline for island water and sewerage works. After a recess (10:18-11:00) all three items were voted on and passed, and the sitting closed at 11:12. The minutes text is partly garbled, so some speech gists are approximate.

Attendance of members

items.title: Announcements from the chair: committee sitting schedules and items sent to committees
Zakat Bill (government bill, sponsored by Vilifushi member Hassan Waheed)
Economic Committee report on the Maldives Intellectual Property Office Bill
items.outcome: debated; third reading and vote later; passed 68-0

items.title: Finance Committee report on the special audit of diesel purchases for Maldives Ports Limited operations, 2018 to 2020
Environment and Climate Change Committee report on the bill to amend the Water and Sewerage Act (Law 8/2020), sponsored by Dhidhdhoo member Abdul Latheef Mohamed
Votes on items
items.outcome: all three items passed; sitting adjourned to 12 August 2025 at 09:00

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Backed the Intellectual Property Office Bill as important for protecting inventions, designs and brands.
Said the ports audit covers 2018-2020 and linked it to the MDP-era administration; urged action.
Supported the water and sewerage amendment and disputed opposition figures on how many islands have the systems.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said theft from state companies has gone on under all governments and urged the government to arrest those responsible.
Said island water and sewerage works have not progressed despite the legal deadline, and criticised extending it.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Raised concern that a new Intellectual Property Office would be run by a minister, and criticised ministers not attending the Majlis to answer questions.
Opposed extending the water and sewerage deadline and questioned a recent Decentralisation Act amendment involving a MVR 10 million threshold.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Presented the Economic Committee report on the Intellectual Property Office Bill, noting the committee amended it and passed it unanimously.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said the committee reviewed the Intellectual Property Office Bill with opposition input and hoped its benefits reach the public soon.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Presented the Finance Committee report and its recommendations on oil purchases and monitoring at Maldives Ports Limited.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Thanked the committee, said MVR 28 million was lost at the ports company, and said the government is taking action.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Called for an independent audit and evaluation of company deals and said systems are needed to stop corruption.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the reports and said fighting corruption needs both government action and individual responsibility.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Said theft from public money has become common, called for proper punishment, and urged reports like this to come before the Majlis more often.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Welcomed the government examining the audit and criticised how past administrations handled public funds.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Said the government is acting on corruption and criticised the opposition's approach.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Presented the Environment and Climate Change Committee report on the Water and Sewerage Act amendment, including a three-month period to make regulations.

decisions: Zakat Bill had its first reading.
Maldives Intellectual Property Office Bill passed at third reading, 68 for, 0 against.
Finance Committee report on the Maldives Ports Limited diesel audit was adopted, 69 for, 0 against.
Bill to amend the Water and Sewerage Act (Law 8/2020) passed, 61 for, 7 against.
Next sitting set for 12 August 2025 at 09:00.
